appraisal.note: AETERNUS editorial judgement; not presented as a historical quotation.

en.tagline: A soldier’s life, written close to its subject.
en.intro: Arthur’s Life of Lord Kitchener gives the career of a commander the breadth of a substantial biography. Campaigns, administration and the machinery of imperial service are gathered around the public figure.
en.orientation: A biography written near its subject’s circle has a particular historical value. Access and sympathy can illuminate the record while also shaping its defence.
career: Arthur’s military background informed his biographical work. His Kitchener volumes appeared in 1920, only four years after their subject’s death.
literature: The three-volume design allows campaigns and administrative work to unfold at length. The biographer’s selection and judgement remain part of what the reader must examine.
en.legacy: The book preserves an early construction of Kitchener’s public memory. It belongs among the sources through which that reputation can be studied.
en.bridge: The separate volumes open successive parts of a large military and administrative career.
